approachQuestion.prompt:
Finish independent workloads

There are n positive integer workloads. At integer speed s>=1, one worker processes each workload separately, taking ceil(workload/s) whole ticks per workload; unused capacity in a tick cannot transfer to another workload. Given H>=n, return the minimum speed completing all work in at most H ticks. 1<=n<=200000; workloads<=10^9; n<=H<=10^14. Examples: [5,5], H=3 -> 5; [7], H=3 -> 3. Prefer scalable worst-case time, then memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Binary-search s from 1 through maximum workload. At each speed sum integer ceilings for every workload; retain the first speed whose sum is <=H.
options.feedback: The feasibility sum decreases with speed; per-workload rounding is essential and cannot be replaced by rounding one total.

options.text: Run the same binary search, first storing the tick count for every workload in a fresh array for each candidate speed.
options.feedback: Correct sums produce the same answer, but the temporary tick array is unnecessary; a running total suffices.

options.text: Return ceil(sum(workloads)/H), assuming unused tick capacity can transfer between workloads.
options.feedback: For [5,5], H=3 this returns 4, but each workload takes two ticks at speed 4, exceeding H.

Round each workload's required time upward separately before summing. Combining workloads before rounding would permit sharing fractional capacity the task forbids. Increasing speed never increases total required time.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. M is maximum workload. Include the initial maximum scan and every full feasibility pass; integer ceilings use overflow-safe signed 64-bit arithmetic. Iterative search, no copied arrays or recursion. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

options.text: O(n log(M + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(n log(M + 1)) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each speed test scans all workloads; include the initial maximum scan.
details: Finding maximum M costs O(n). O(log(M+1)) speed candidates each require a full n-workload ceiling sum, giving O(n log(M+1)). Only speed bounds, the current workload, and accumulated time remain live.
“O(n log(M + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The feasibility sum decreases with speed; per-workload rounding is essential and cannot be replaced by rounding one total.
“O(n log(M + 1)) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space”: The maximum scan and full feasibility passes reuse workload input and scalar totals, not an n-entry copied array.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Even one feasibility evaluation can inspect every workload, and the searched speed range adds repeated evaluations.
